entries.name: Cook's Assistant
entries.summary: The head cook of Lumbridge Castle forgot to buy the ingredients for Duke Horacio's birthday cake and roped in the first adventurer through the kitchen door. That was you. An egg, a bucket of milk and a pot of flour later he kept his job, and you got the use of his special range, the Cook-o-matic 100.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
You walked into the kitchen on the ground floor of Lumbridge Castle and found the head cook in a panic. It was the Duke of Lumbridge's birthday, the cook was meant to be baking the cake, and he had forgotten to buy the ingredients. He was certain the Duke would sack him, and he had four children and a goat to feed. His words; I have a note on the goat further down.

The list was a bucket of milk, an egg and a pot of flour. He pointed you to Millie Miller at Mill Lane Mill for the flour, Gillie Groats at the cow field across the river for the milk, and the Groats' farm or any chicken for the egg. Any chicken. He was past being particular.

The egg first. You went east from the castle and north up the path to the chicken coop north-west of Farmer Fred's house and picked one up. Nothing to it.

Then the milk. You took an empty bucket into the cow field and used it on the dairy cow, the one wearing a cowbell. There is always a bucket in the castle cellar, and the general store sells them if you would rather not go down a trapdoor. Gillie Groats will explain milking if asked; it is a cow and a bucket, but the offer stands.

Then the flour, which took the most steps. You took an empty pot to the wheat field and picked grain; there is always one on the kitchen table. You carried it into Mill Lane Mill, tipped it into the hopper on the top floor, pulled the lever, and filled the pot from the flour bin on the ground floor. Millie Miller inside the mill explains how it works, should the lever not explain itself.

You brought all three back and the cook declared himself saved. You asked whether you could come to the Duke's party. He said only important people dine with nobility, and that perhaps one day you would be one of them, though he doubted it. I have underlined 'doubted'.

Then he let you use his range. He calls it the Cook-o-matic 100, and it burns fewer foods than an ordinary range. Somebody in that kitchen needed to. Rewards: 1 quest point, 300 Cooking experience and the use of the Cook-o-matic 100.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Cook (Lumbridge), head cook of Lumbridge Castle, described, with no great effort, as "The head cook of Lumbridge castle." He needed an egg, milk and flour for the Duke's cake and was sure he would be sacked for the lack of them. He kept the job, and asks for your help again in Recipe for Disaster. He claims a wife, four children and a goat, which Bob the cat contradicts, and he admits he has burned every cake he has ever tried to bake.

Duke Horacio, the Duke of Lumbridge, whose birthday it was. Never seen during the quest; he lives on the first floor of the castle, one floor up from the trouble. He is a direct descendant of Polonius, the first Duke.

Gillie Groats, the milkmaid at the cow field across the River Lum. Optional. She explains how to milk a cow, should you want it explained.

Millie Miller, at Mill Lane Mill. Optional. She explains how grain becomes flour, which is the one worth hearing.

Farmer Fred, not spoken to. His house is the landmark for the chicken coop, and that was the whole of his part.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Lumbridge Castle kitchen, ground floor. The cook, his range, and a pot that is always on the centre table.

Lumbridge Castle cellar, down the kitchen trapdoor. There is always a bucket.

The chicken coop north-west of Farmer Fred's house. The egg.

The Lumbridge cow field. The dairy cow with the cowbell; Gillie Groats stands across the River Lum.

The wheat field south-west of the cow field. The grain.

Mill Lane Mill. Hopper and lever on the top floor, flour bin on the ground floor, Millie Miller inside.

Lumbridge General Store. Buckets and pots, if you arrive with neither.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The errand sends a newcomer all round Lumbridge. A shopping list doing the work of a map. It works.

The cook has form. It came out later that he has tried and failed to bake a cake countless times, which is why he keeps needing new adventurers. In Death to the Dorgeshuun, when you introduce Zanik to him, he tries to offer her the very same errand, eggs, flour and milk for the Duke's birthday cake. You tell him she has no time and he says it was worth a try.

The histories take this to mean he asks every newcomer. I take it the same way. The cook at the Servants' Guild in Ardougne complains that she was fired overnight and replaced by a fool who cannot bake a cake without help. The description fits.

The kitchen has history. The cook's ancestor Franizzard Van Lumbcook won the post of head cook for life a century ago by impressing the Lumbridge council with a banquet. In Recipe for Disaster, which follows on from this one, the cook tries to recreate that banquet for the council's ten-yearly meeting. The Culinaromancer, a hostile cook trapped in another dimension a hundred years earlier, crashes the feast.

Lumbridge itself was settled in 1937 of the Fourth Age by human nomads who bridged the River Lum, which is where the name comes from. Polonius was the first Duke, given the land by King Claudius of Varrock, and he replaced the original wooden fort with Lumbridge Castle. Duke Horacio is his direct descendant. Caves beneath the town sheltered a lost goblin tribe during the God Wars, which nobody in the kitchen brought up.

On the range. Cook-o-matic 100 is the cook's own name for it; adventurers call it the Lumbridge Castle range. It lowers the odds of burning many foods, from bread and shrimps up to anglerfish and admiral pie, and is especially good for mushroom and botanical pies.

Bob the cat praises the cook's old fashioned seafood gumbo, an old family recipe. So the man can cook. He cannot bake, which is a different complaint.

One last note. You can buy all three ingredients on the Grand Exchange before talking to the cook and finish the quest in seconds. Which rather defeats the map.

people: Cook (Lumbridge) - head cook, forgot the ingredients, kept the job
Duke Horacio - Duke of Lumbridge, the birthday, never seen
Gillie Groats - milkmaid at the cow field, optional
Millie Miller - miller at Mill Lane Mill, optional
Farmer Fred - not spoken to, his house marks the chicken coop
places: Lumbridge Castle - kitchen and cellar
Chicken coop - north-west of Farmer Fred's house, the egg
Lumbridge cow field - dairy cow with a cowbell, the milk
Wheat field - south-west of the cow field, the grain
Mill Lane Mill - hopper upstairs, flour bin below, the flour
Lumbridge General Store - buckets and pots, if short
River Lum - Gillie Groats stands across it
details: A shopping list doing the work of a map; the errand sends a newcomer all round Lumbridge
Four children and a goat, says the cook; Bob the cat says otherwise
He tries to give Zanik the same errand in Death to the Dorgeshuun, worth a try, he says
He has failed to bake a cake countless times, it came out later, hence the adventurers
The Ardougne Servants' Guild cook says she was replaced by him, overnight
The Cook-o-matic 100 is his name for it; best known as the Lumbridge range
The cook's ancestor Franizzard Van Lumbcook sets up Recipe for Disaster
All three ingredients are on the Grand Exchange, and the quest takes seconds

entries.name: Priest in Peril
entries.summary: King Roald sent you to look in on Drezel, priest of Paterdomus on the River Salve, because the temple had gone quiet. Monks of Zamorak had taken it, and they talked you into killing the Temple Guardian so they could poison the river; that part is in the minutes, I am afraid. You freed Drezel, sealed a vampyre in its coffin with blessed water, soaked the poison out of the Salve with rune essence, and Drezel opened the way into Morytania.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
King Roald saw you in the south-east room of Varrock Palace. Word had stopped coming from the temple to Saradomin on Misthalin's eastern border. That temple is Paterdomus, and it guards the only passage into the vampyre-infested land of Morytania; the blessed waters of the River Salve beneath it are what keep the vampyres out.

The priest there, Drezel, is descended from the warriors who blessed the river, and nobody had heard from him. Roald asked you to go and check on him. I wrote down 'check'. It turned out to be a small word for the job.

We went north-east through Silvarea, past the Earth altar, to the temple door. A voice asked who you were and what you wanted. When you said the King had sent you, a second voice introduced itself as Drevil, then hurriedly corrected that to Drezel. I wrote 'Drevil' down with a question mark, and nobody consulted the notes.

This so-called Drezel said a horrible big dog-like thing had moved into the mausoleum outside and asked you to get rid of it. Down the trapdoor north of the temple you killed the Temple Guardian, a level 30 dog. Magic does nothing to it, nor does a dwarf cannon, and it never comes back. A ring of recoil will do it, so long as you land at least one point of damage yourself.

Back at the palace, King Roald was furious. The dog was no pest: it guarded the mausoleum entrance and the source of the Salve, and with it dead anyone could sabotage the river's blessing and leave the whole of Misthalin open to the vampyres. He called it treason and threatened to have you beheaded, then relented and ordered you to put it right. I took those minutes very quietly.

You picked up a bucket and went back. The palace bedroom has one, or the general store sells them for 2 coins. Inside the temple you fought the hooded level 30 Monk of Zamorak, who casts spells, though there is a spot between the pews he cannot reach you in, and took the golden key he dropped.

Upstairs was the real Drezel, locked in a cell. Through the bars he told you Zamorakians had attacked the temple, meaning to desecrate the blessing the Seven Priestly Warriors had placed on the holy River Salve and leave Misthalin defenceless against the vampyres of Morytania. They had also brought a trapped vampyre up into a coffin near his cell. The golden key did not fit his door; the Zamorakians had hidden the real one somewhere.

Back in the mausoleum, the golden key opened a southern gate into a room with seven monuments around a well. Searching the monuments turned up the iron key, which you swapped for the golden one. The other monuments hold a golden pot, feather, candle, tinderbox, needle and hammer, which can be swapped once as souvenirs before Drezel moves. You filled the bucket with murky water from the well, and murky was the polite word.

The iron key opened Drezel's cell. He blessed the water and you poured it over the coffin outside his cell, sealing the vampyre inside. Then he asked you to meet him below, in the mausoleum, to help repair what the Zamorakians had done.

In the north-east passage under the temple, Drezel explained that the Zamorakians had used a potion to pollute the River Salve. While he worked on reinforcing the barrier between Morytania and Misthalin, he needed you to soak up the evil magic the potion had released into the water. That meant fifty rune essence or pure essence, in one trip with pouches or several without. Hand him the essence outright and he skips the speech; what gets written is that you gave the priest your blank runes, which I have not corrected.

When it was done he thanked you and gave you Wolfbane, a silver dagger passed down through his family for generations and imbued with the power of Saradomin. He blessed you to pass the barrier, warned of the vampyres and werewolves beyond, and mentioned the Myreque resistance. To actually cross you must ask him for permission to pass and wait for his blessing; he is a priest, and there is a form.

For your trouble: 1 quest point, 1,406 Prayer experience, Wolfbane, the way into Canifis and Morytania, and 5 Kudos from Historian Minas at the Varrock Museum. The dagger gets its own paragraph further down. It earned it.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
King Roald: King Roald Remanis III, ruler of Misthalin, in Varrock Palace, married to Queen Ellamaria; he sent you to check on Drezel, threatened you with execution when the guardian died, then gave you the chance to fix it. The histories call him a straightforward, stable ruler under whom Varrock has prospered. The notes on the guardian have him calling the dog Spots and a pedigree light beast, or possibly dark beast. He was not sure which.

Drezel: described, and briefly, as "A holy man." Priest of Saradomin, the temple's only monk, and descended from one of the Seven Priestly Warriors; the Zamorakians locked him in a cell on the top floor. After the quest he lives in the passage beneath Paterdomus, where he starts Nature Spirit, replaces lost Wolfbane daggers, blesses travellers to cross the river, and later works with the Myreque in In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale and Sins of the Father. Use a spare iron key on his old cell door and he asks what you are trying to lock him back in for, which is a fair question.

Monk of Zamorak (hooded, level 30): the impostor at the door who slipped and said Drevil, tricked you into killing the guardian, and dropped the golden key. Described as "An evil human cleric." The other monks in the temple heal quickly and give only 25 percent of normal combat experience. Not worth the trouble.

Temple Guardian: described, and fairly, as "Looks like a big ugly dog." Level 30, 45 hitpoints, hits for 3 at most, and stabs. It guarded the mausoleum entrance and the source of the Salve, and it does not come back. The description was unkind; so, in the end, were we.

The coffin vampyre: one of the vampyres caught on the Misthalin side when the Salve was blessed, too weak to be a threat but impossible to kill, so the Saradominists kept it sealed in a coffin. You sealed it again with blessed water. It did not thank you.

Historian Minas: at the Varrock Museum, gives 5 Kudos for the quest. He did not ask to see my notes. Nobody does.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Varrock Palace: King Roald's audience room, in the south-east corner by the main entrance. There is always a bucket in the palace bedroom.

Silvarea: the mountain pass in north-east Misthalin, past the Earth altar, ending at the temple.

Paterdomus: the temple on the River Salve. An altar on the ground floor, monks of Zamorak above, Drezel's cell and the coffin on the top floor, more coffins outside.

The mausoleum: down the trapdoor north of the temple. The guardian's chamber, the seven-monument room with the well, and the north-east passage where Drezel settles.

The River Salve: the blessed river that forms Misthalin's border with Morytania. The temple bridge is the only crossing.

Morytania and Canifis: the werewolf town just east of the temple, opened by the quest. More on both below.

Varrock Museum: Historian Minas and the Kudos.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The blessing on the Salve was not what the soldiers were told. The Misthalin-Morytania War ran from about 1100 to 1200 of the Fourth Age, when Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan, vampyre ruler of Morytania, crossed the Salve to expand west and pushed towards Varrock. The Temple Knights sent the Seven Priestly Warriors to secure the river and, secretly, to research haemalchemy for a weakness in the vampyres. Their names: Ivandis Seergaze, Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious, Friar Twiblick and Essiandar Gar.

At the river's source they performed a blood ritual as the vampyres attacked. Derygull fell first, the rest followed, and only Ivandis survived. He laid them to rest around the well where the ritual was done, and the temple was later built around it. The warriors hid the profane nature of the ritual from the soldiers and presented it as a holy consecration; later accounts say it sealed the vengeful power of Saradomin in the river.

Ivandis was showing signs of vampyrification. He refused to become the thing he had fought and made a suicide run at Drakan; he died, and was laid in a coffin in tunnels beneath the Hollows in Morytania. He came from what is now Lumbridge, and Ivan Strom is his last living descendant. That last part should be better known.

The blessed water burns creatures of Zamorak on contact and keeps vampyres from crossing. Any vampyres already on the Misthalin side were left severely weakened but could not be killed, so they were sealed in coffins outside the temple. Werewolves can still cross, and do, kidnapping people and smuggling for the vampyres; some have got as far as beneath the Champions' Guild. After Drakan's defeat he banished his brother Draynor, likely because of the weakness the blessed river imposed.

The Salve flows past where Senntisten, the old Zarosian capital, once stood; the Digsite excavations reach its bank. Blessed water seeping through the rock of the Mort Ridge Mine forms Salve shards, crystals with power over evil. The river has more history than most kingdoms.

Paterdomus is from the old tongue: pater, father, and domus, house, roughly House of the Father, for Saradomin. It stands in eastern Silvarea on the River Salve and was built on the site of the last battle of the Misthalin-Morytania War, over the graves of the warriors who blessed the river. The notes on Silvarea add that the warriors rest under the temple, which was built in their honour.

Morytania was once the Hallowland, a peaceful Saradominist kingdom ruled by the Icyene queen Efaritay. Drakan, a true-born vampyre brought from Vampyrium by Zaros in the Second Age, sided with Zamorak in exchange for these lands and conquered them in the Third Age with vampyres and werewolves. He captured Efaritay's husband Ascertes, who became the vampyre Vanstrom Klause, and turned the kingdom into a blood farm.

He built the capital Darkmeyer on Hallowvale's ruins and made Meiyerditch a blood-tithed ghetto; Burgh de Rott is the last free human town and home of the Myreque resistance. He rules with his siblings Vanescula and Ranis.

Canifis, just east of the temple, was the Zarosian fortress Kharyrll before the God Wars. Werewolves settled it in year 23 of the Fifth Age and pay blood tithes like everyone else in Morytania. The name is probably from canis, the old word for a wolf and its kin.

Its twenty citizens turn into level 88 werewolves when attacked unless you wield Wolfbane. Mazchna the Slayer master and Roavar the barman live there. Lovely people. Mind the teeth.

Wolfbane: "A silver dagger that can prevent werewolves changing form." It strikes like a mithril dagger, with a 5 Prayer bonus on top, cannot be poisoned, and as a silver weapon works on tier 1 vampyres. You can only hold one, and Drezel replaces it. Killing a Canifis citizen with it counts for the Easy Morytania Diary.

Drezel next sends you into Mort Myre Swamp with meat and apple pies for the druid Filliman Tarlock in Nature Spirit, which also needs The Restless Ghost. Priest in Peril is required for Animal Magnetism, Creature of Fenkenstrain, Desert Treasure I, Ghosts Ahoy, Haunted Mine, His Faithful Servants, Making History, Nature Spirit, Rum Deal, Shades of Mort'ton and Wanted! The monks of Zamorak were finally driven out of Paterdomus for good in The Blood Moon Rises, the quest in which Drakan is slain. That took a while.

One loose end. If you carry a clue scroll that wants Drezel, he sees to the clue in the mausoleum before he gets on with the quest. It does not matter much. It is true, so it stays.

people: King Roald - King Roald Remanis III of Misthalin, sent you, then threatened to behead you
Drezel - priest of Saradomin, found in a cell at Paterdomus
Monk of Zamorak - hooded impostor, said Drevil once, dropped the golden key
Temple Guardian - the dog you were tricked into killing
Historian Minas - 5 Kudos at the Varrock Museum, no questions asked
Ivandis Seergaze - only survivor of the Seven Priestly Warriors
Lord Drakan - vampyre ruler of Morytania, in the histories only
Queen Ellamaria - Roald's wife, not met
places: Varrock Palace - south-east room, where it started
Silvarea - the pass past the Earth altar
Paterdomus - the temple on the River Salve
Mausoleum - trapdoor north of the temple, well and monuments
River Salve - blessed border with Morytania
Canifis - werewolf town, opened by the quest
Morytania - the vampyre lands beyond
Varrock Museum - Kudos from Historian Minas
details: The impostor at the door slips and calls himself Drevil. I noticed.
King Roald's nickname for the Temple Guardian was Spots
Paterdomus means, roughly, House of the Father
Only Ivandis survived the ritual; he died charging Drakan
Vampyres stranded west of the Salve were sealed in coffins
The Salve flows past the ruins of Senntisten
Canifis was the Zarosian fortress Kharyrll
Wolfbane strikes like a mithril dagger, with a Prayer bonus on top
The monks were finally cleared out in The Blood Moon Rises

entries.name: Waterfall Quest
entries.summary: Almera asked you to fetch her son Hudon back from treasure hunting on the river at Baxtorian Falls. You never did get him home, but you learned the legend of the elven king Baxtorian and his lost queen Glarial, took her amulet and urn from her tomb, and carried her ashes into Baxtorian's sealed home under the falls. Tipping the ashes into the Chalice of Eternity gave up his treasure, so I have filed the errand as a success, loosely.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body:
Almera, in her house north-east of Baxtorian Falls and south of the Barbarian Outpost, was worried about her son Hudon. He had gone looking for treasure on the river behind the house, cannot swim, and had already fallen in three times. You took her log raft, which wrecked on a small island, and there he was. He refused to come home, said he would find the treasure soon, and turned down your help on the grounds that you would only steal it.

You swam south and washed ashore near a large building with a fisherman, Gerald, outside: the Tourist Information Centre, where Hadley works. Upstairs, the southernmost bookcase on the east wall held the Book on Baxtorian, which you had to read, and I read over your shoulder. It says Baxtorian and Glarial were elves, that a treasure lies under the falls, and that Glarial's pebble, the key to her tomb, was taken by a gnome family over a century ago, whose descendants might still keep it in their cave beneath the Tree Gnome Village. Gerald and Hadley tell the same story between them: an ancient elven king who shut himself in his secret home under the waterfall after his wife was captured and killed by invaders.

Next the Tree Gnome Village, south-west of Ardougne, through the hedge maze past the hobgoblins and down the ladder into the dungeon. In the east room a key sat in a differently coloured crate in the south-east corner. In the west room the gnome Golrie had locked himself in to keep the hobgoblins off his family's heirlooms, and had left the key outside. You let him out and he handed over Glarial's pebble as a bit of old elven junk, keeping the key so he could lock up again.

Glarial's Tomb lies south-east of the falls and north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. The stone says Glarial, wife of Baxtorian and a true friend of nature, rests knowing only visitors with peaceful intent may enter, and it means it: the pebble only opens the tomb if you carry no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition. Inside, three level 84 Moss Guardians roam alongside zombies and skeletons. You took Glarial's amulet from the chest in the west chamber and Glarial's urn, holding her ashes, from the coffin in the south chamber, and the tomb will not let you leave without both.

Back to Almera's, the raft again, and the wreck again. You tied your rope to the big grey rock downstream, then used it on a dead tree to climb up to the doors on the waterfall ledge. Wearing Glarial's amulet is what stops the door washing you out. The eastern passage, past level 52 Shadow spiders, level 45 Skeletons and level 16 Skeleton Mages, had a key in the northernmost crate; the western passage led past level 86 Fire giants to a locked door and the chalice room.

The final chamber holds six pillars, two statues and the Chalice of Eternity, floating in the air. You used one air, one water and one earth rune on each of the six pillars, Glarial's amulet on the statue of Glarial, and the urn on the chalice, tipping her ashes in. The ground rose. I put the quill down for that part.

Baxtorian's treasure was yours: 2 diamonds, 2 gold bars and 40 mithril seeds, with 13,750 Attack and 13,750 Strength experience and 1 quest point. Try to take it without the ritual and you are washed out of the cavern, and you lose the amulet and the urn. As for Hudon, the errand itself, he never was rescued. He still has not found anything, and insists you owe him a share, since he showed you where the treasure was.

sections.heading: Who was there
sections.body:
Almera: described, and fairly, as "Nice hair." Hudon's mother, living at the falls south of the Barbarian Outpost, and where the quest starts. Speedy Keith gets the very same words. I checked twice.

Hudon: described as "Looks young." Ran away to hunt for treasure under the falls. He cannot be rescued, which was the whole errand, and afterwards accuses you of stealing his treasure. I have not warmed to him.

Gerald: described as "Looks suspiciously like a fisherman." Fishes trout and salmon south of the falls by the River Dougne. He knows the story of the treasure said to have been left by the elven king Baxtorian about 200 years earlier, at the end of the Fourth Age, and that many adventurers have searched for his tomb and failed. He was glad of someone to tell it to.

Hadley: described, not by me, as "Could do with losing a bit of weight." The tourist guide at the Tourist Information Centre by Lake Baxtorian, where the Book on Baxtorian is kept upstairs. He turns up again in Desert Treasure I, helping to find the Shadow Dungeon.

Golrie: described as "He seems to be in a spot of bother." A gnome in the Tree Gnome Village dungeon, grandson of King Bolrie and grand-nephew of King Bolren, who locked himself in against the hobgoblins after leaving the key outside. He gives Glarial's pebble, and replacements if you lose it, and turns up again in The Path of Glouphrie. After Roving Elves the hobgoblins are the ones locked up, and the word on him becomes "No longer locked in his own cage."

Baxtorian: Lord Baxtorian Cadarn, formerly King Baxtorian, the Fourth Age elven king who led the Cadarn clan east through Arandar to found a kingdom in what is now Kandarin. Husband of Glarial, father of Eirlys. He sealed himself under the falls in grief, and you do not meet him in this quest. In Song of the Elves he turns out to be alive, turned to stone in the hope of one day reuniting with Glarial; he is freed and, reluctantly, becomes elder of the Cadarn clan.

Glarial: Queen Glarial, Baxtorian's wife, mother of Eirlys and grandmother of Islwyn. After Seren shattered herself, she and Baxtorian were entrusted with leading the elves. She ruled the eastern kingdom while Baxtorian marched on Prifddinas, was captured when it fell, and was never recovered alive; the elves later buried her ashes in the tomb under the protection of the Moss Guardians. Taking her urn leaves her spirit restless until Roving Elves, and that one is on us.

Moss Guardians: described as "Bigger than your average moss giant." The guardian spirits of Glarial's Tomb: level 84, 120 hitpoints, hits up to 14, and swings slowly, a blow first and then magic behind it. Fought unarmed, since the tomb allows nothing else. Killed again in Roving Elves for a consecration seed.

Fire giants: described as "A very large elemental adversary." Level 86 in the Waterfall Dungeon, hits up to 11, and there are eleven of them. The strongest of the ordinary giants.

Also met: Shadow spiders (level 52, drain Prayer, and do not show on the map), Skeletons (45) and Skeleton Mages (16) in the dungeon, and hobgoblins (28) in the gnome dungeon.

sections.heading: Where it took us
sections.body:
Almera's house: north-east of Baxtorian Falls, south of the Barbarian Outpost, with the raft beside it.

Baxtorian Falls: rapids running south from the Lunar Sea to the River Dougne, north-west of Ardougne and east of the Tree Gnome Stronghold, named for Baxtorian. The small island is where the raft wrecks. Both times.

Tourist Information Centre: just south of the falls by Lake Baxtorian. Hadley inside, Gerald fishing outside, the Book on Baxtorian upstairs.

Tree Gnome Village: south-east of East Ardougne and north of Yanille, hidden inside a hedge maze.

Tree Gnome Village Dungeon: under the maze. East room with the key crate, zombies and giant bats; west room with Golrie and the hobgoblins.

Glarial's Tomb: south-east of the falls, north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. The west chest and the south coffin.

Waterfall Dungeon: the connected caverns under the falls. The ledge doors, the eastern passage with spiders, skeletons and the key crate, the western passage with fire giants, and the Chalice of Eternity in the northernmost cavern.

Barbarian Outpost and Fishing Guild: the landmarks either side of the falls. Good for bearings.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The reason for the sealed door is the Elven Civil War. After the God Wars Seren shattered herself, and Baxtorian led the Cadarn clan, the military clan, east through the Arandar pass. He made non-aggression pacts with the gnomes and humans, and the kingdom prospered for nearly 1,900 years. Around 1930 of the Fourth Age, contact with Tirannwn ceased.

The Iorwerth clan had seized Prifddinas while most of the army was away, leaving thousands dead. They had become obsessed with a Dark Lord, who the elves believed was Zamorak but who turns out to be a fragment of Seren. Baxtorian spent five years besieging the city, whose walls Seren had built to withstand gods. His soldiers found a secret entrance and rescued the imprisoned clan elders.

Meanwhile his eastern kingdom fell to invaders, most of his people were slaughtered and Glarial was taken. He chased her captors into caves south of the ruined kingdom, into what was clearly a trap, and lost his remaining soldiers. Broken, he sealed himself in the home he had built for Glarial beneath the falls. The other elders reverted Prifddinas to a crystal seed, and Lletya was founded as a refuge under Arianwyn.

The war ended in year 169 of the Fifth Age with Song of the Elves, where Baxtorian is freed, Prifddinas is restored and Lord Iorwerth dies. On who took Glarial, the accounts disagree. The account of Glarial calls her captors unknown enemies, the account of the war says human invaders, and Islwyn in Roving Elves blames humans for her death. I have kept all three.

The book deserves its own note. Its own title is The Missing Relics, and it is described as "A book on elven history in northern Gielinor." It says many elven relics were lost when the elves left in the Fourth Age, and that dwarf miners may have taken Baxtorian's treasure early in the Fifth Age. It also says only Baxtorian and Glarial had the power to enter the falls, and the enchantment has kept everyone else out.

Inside is a sonnet on the love between Baxtorian and Glarial, which lasted over a century while they taught the laws of nature. There is a section on their power over nature, commanding trees to grow, hills to rise and rivers to flood, with Baxtorian a master of rune lore who used stones to control water, earth and air. That is why the pillars take air, water and earth runes. There is also Baxtorian's own Ode to Eternity, on which I offer no opinion.

It can be displayed in your own house or read in the Grand Library of Prifddinas.

Roving Elves picks the story up, once both Waterfall Quest and Regicide are behind you. Islwyn, Glarial's grumpy grandson, and the kind young elf Eluned scout for the rebel elves in Isafdar. Glarial's spirit is restless because you took her urn, so you fetch a consecration seed by killing a Moss Guardian unarmed in her tomb and consecrate her new resting place in the Waterfall Dungeon. Golrie gives a new pebble if yours is lost, and once that quest starts he and the hobgoblins swap places.

Desert Treasure I, Legends' Quest, Roving Elves and The Path of Glouphrie all wait on this one, and so does the Medium Kandarin Diary. The Chalice comes up again in Biohazard, where King Lathas claims his brother Tyras was corrupted when the Dark Lord forced him to drink from it. That is a lie, and I have it written down as one, told to turn you against Tyras. There is no evidence the Chalice has anything to do with the Dark Lord.

Odds and ends from the margin. There is a barrel at the falls that drops you straight into the dungeon, if you are the sort. A second waterfall flows east out of the lake. Rasolo the merchant sells overpriced goods south of the falls by the Tourist Information Centre, and rumours say dwarven miners found Baxtorian's treasure years ago.

A statue of Baxtorian stands at the falls monument. Glarial's amulet looks identical to the gnome amulet. Golrie's great-uncle King Bolren rules the Tree Gnome Village and fights General Khazard's army in the Tree Gnome Village quest.

For the minutes: no skill is asked of you, and it can be done at level 3. The experience takes Attack and Strength from 1 to 30, and a level 3 adventurer to 22. The dungeon's fire giants are the old reliable source of rune scimitars, at about one in a hundred and twenty-eight, by my tallies. Once you have both the quest and the medium Kandarin Diary behind you, no rope is needed.

entries.name: Giant Mole
entries.summary: A mole the size of a hay cart, living in the tunnels under Falador Park. Wyson the gardener grew it by accident with a bottle of growth potion, which is the kind of accident I keep notes on. You reach it by digging into the mole hills with a spade.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The Giant Mole, or Talpidae wysonian if you want the scientific name. Level 230, three tiles across, and a fairly simple fight as these things go. The note on it just reads "Holy Mole-y!" I did not write that.

Its main trick is to burrow off through the tunnels when it is hurt. It also puts out any candle, torch or oil lamp you are carrying if it comes up close enough to reach you. Annoying, but consistent.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Mole Hole, under Falador Park. Dig with a spade on one of the mole hills in the park and you drop straight in.

The tunnels are dark. Without a light you will be hurt as you walk them, so bring one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The histories put its origin down as a slight accident. Wyson the gardener poured a bottle of Malignius-Mortifer's-Super-Ultra-Flora-Growth-Potion on his plants. The name of the potion should have been a warning.

It always drops a mole skin and a mole claw, and Wyson trades those for bird nests, which is a tidy arrangement for the man who caused the problem. Killing it once is a hard Falador Diary task.

people: Wyson the gardener - the Falador Park gardener whose potion accident created it. Trades mole skins and claws for bird nests.
Malignius Mortifer - source of the growth potion that started all this.
places: Falador Park - the mole hills on the surface are the way in. Bring a spade.
Mole Hole - the tunnels under the park where the fight happens. Dark.
details: Scientific name Talpidae wysonian, after Wyson
Retreats through the tunnels when damaged. Follow the falling dirt
Puts out candles, torches and oil lamps when it surfaces close by
Always drops a mole skin and a mole claw
One kill completes a hard Falador Diary task

plates.caption: Falador, with a mole under it.

entries.name: King Black Dragon
entries.summary: A black dragon with three heads, and one of the biggest, meanest dragons around. It was the strongest creature known in the old days. Its lair sits behind a lever in the deep Wilderness, which tells you most of what you need to know.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Level 276, three heads, and the size of a house. People describe it as "One of the biggest, meanest dragons around." They are not exaggerating.

It has four breaths: ordinary dragonfire, then shock, ice and poison. It will set on you unprovoked and its bite poisons. Its weakness is water spells, which seems fair for something that breathes fire.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The King Black Dragon Lair, reached through the deep Wilderness near the Lava Maze. Climb down the ladder near the lesser demons, then pull the lever surrounded by poisonous spiders. The lair itself is not Wilderness. The approach very much is.

Common routes in: a burning amulet to the Lava Maze, the lever north-west of Ardougne Castle to the Deserted Keep, the Edgeville canoe, or the Wilderness obelisks. 50,000 coins buys you the lair to yourself. Steep, but nobody else gets a swing at your dragon.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
For a long while it was the strongest creature anyone in Gielinor had met, and it held that title until the Kalphite Queen turned up. I have that in the margin, underlined.

It can talk. In A Tail of Two Cats it holds a conversation with Bob the cat, and gets interrupted before it finishes. I would have liked the minutes of that one.

Rare drops include the KBD heads, the dragon pickaxe, the draconic visage and the prince black dragon pet. Each of those gets its own footnote.

people: Bob the cat - talks with the dragon in A Tail of Two Cats. Interrupted, sadly.
Krystilia - her black dragon tasks do not count the King Black Dragon. Check before you set off.
places: King Black Dragon Lair - the fight itself, outside the Wilderness proper
Lava Maze - the deep Wilderness approach, with the ladder near the lesser demons
Deserted Keep - reached by the Ardougne lever, a fast way north
Edgeville - where the canoe route starts
details: Three heads, four breath types: dragonfire, shock, ice and poison
Strongest creature known, once, until the Kalphite Queen
Speaks in A Tail of Two Cats
KBD heads about one in 128, dragon pickaxe one in 1,000, prince black dragon pet one in 3,000, draconic visage one in 5,000, by my tallies

Lair to yourself, 50,000 coins

entries.name: Goblin
entries.summary: One of the most common low-level creatures in Gielinor, and the first thing most new adventurers ever fight. Goblins are a race the war god Bandos brought to the world. Their main village in Asgarnia is run by two generals who cannot agree on anything, and somehow it still stands.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
One of the most common low-level creatures found around Gielinor. The word on them is "An ugly green creature." Blunt, but not wrong.

Most are level 2 with 5 hitpoints. The armed ones are level 5, and the tougher sort level 13. New adventurers learning to fight go looking for them, which is a polite way of putting it.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Everywhere a new adventurer is likely to tread. Lumbridge alone has over a hundred of them, and there are more between Lumbridge and Varrock, west of Varrock, at the Digsite, Port Sarim, Draynor Village and Lumbridge Swamp.

Further afield too: the Goblin Cave, near the Fishing Guild, the Tree Gnome Village maze, the Clock Tower Dungeon, Hosidius, the Kebos Lowlands, the Hollows, the Observatory Dungeon and the Underground Pass. You are never far from one.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Goblins follow Bandos, the Big High War God. He arrived on Gielinor in the Second Age to wage war, and brought armies of goblins, ogres, orks and ourgs with him. Goblins are not strong. They make up for it with numbers, which is the oldest trick there is.

Goblin Village in Asgarnia is ruled by General Bentnoze of the Thorobshuun tribe and General Wartface of the Garagorshuun tribe. They butt heads over trivial things, armour colours among them. Settling one such argument is the whole of the quest Goblin Diplomacy. Diplomacy is a generous word for it.

Not all goblins went along with it. The Dorgeshuun cave goblins rejected Bandos' doctrines and went back to the cooperative ways of their Yu'biusk past. Sensible, and rare.

people: General Bentnoze - Thorobshuun general of Goblin Village. One half of the argument.
General Wartface - Garagorshuun general of Goblin Village. The other half.
Bandos - the Big High War God the goblins follow. Brought them here in the first place.
places: Lumbridge - the biggest concentration of goblins, over a hundred of them
Goblin Village - the main goblin settlement in Asgarnia, where the generals argue
Dorgesh-Kaan - home of the Dorgeshuun cave goblins, who turned away from Bandos

Bandos brought goblins to Gielinor in the Second Age
Weak on their own, dangerous in numbers
Goblin Diplomacy is about the generals' armour colour argument

entries.name: Hill Giant
entries.summary: A very large foe, found in dungeons and hills across Gielinor. The weakest of the three giant kinds most adventurers meet first, which is not the same as weak. Their giant keys open the door to Obor, the Hill Titan.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
A type of giant, level 28. Described as "A very large foe." Of the Kourend sort they say "A very large foe that has been corrupted by the Dark Altar", which is the same giant in a worse neighbourhood.

They always drop big bones. Now and then one drops a giant key, which opens the fight with Obor, or a giant champion scroll for the Champions' Challenge. Worth checking the pile.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Edgeville Dungeon has the most of them close to home. The Shayzien Giant Pit has more still.

Also in the Giants' Den, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Giants' Plateau, Taverley Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Lava Maze, the Gnome Maze, north of the Observatory, south-west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold, the Bone Yard and the Avium Savannah.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The old histories just call them Giants. The hill was put on the front of the name to keep them apart from the other giant kinds, and it is said the hill is for their arm muscles, which resemble hills. I have looked. I suppose they do.

Despite the name, most of them live in dungeons. Some carry cleavers, which are weapons from Recipe for Disaster. They are one of the three giant kinds most adventurers meet first, alongside moss giants and ice giants, and the weakest of the three.

people: Obor - the Hill Titan. A giant key from a hill giant gets you through his door.
places: Edgeville Dungeon - the biggest gathering close to home, 12 giants
Giant Pit - the Shayzien gathering, 13 giants
Catacombs of Kourend - home of the Dark Altar corrupted sort
Giants' Plateau - has its own sort of hill giant
details: Level 28
Once just called Giants in the old histories
Named for arm muscles that look like hills, or so it is said

entries.name: Fire giant
entries.summary: The strongest of the ordinary giants, a huge elemental brute that lives in the Waterfall Dungeon and a dozen other caves. A favourite Slayer and Ranged target, and the classic source of a rune scimitar. Everyone goes back eventually.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Described as "A very large elemental adversary." Understated. This is the strongest of the ordinary giants, and it is huge.

Three sorts. Level 86 has 111 hitpoints and hits up to 11. Then level 104, then level 109. All of them aggressive, and none of them quick to swing.

Nothing burns it. Water magic bites. No surprises on either count.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The Waterfall Dungeon has eleven. They guard Baxtorian's western passage and the chalice room.

Also the Brimhaven Dungeon, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Charred Dungeon, the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, the Giants' Den, the Isle of Souls Dungeon, the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon, the Smoke Dungeon and the Stronghold Slayer Dungeon.

Most of those spots have a corner it cannot reach you in. The Charred Dungeon is the only one where more than one can set on you at once, so mind yourself there.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
No Slayer level is needed, but the Slayer masters assign them all the same. A favourite Slayer target, and a favourite Ranged one too.

The drop that matters is the rune scimitar, about one in a hundred and twenty-eight by my tallies. The classic place to get one, and the reason for most of the visits. Beyond that: the fire battlestaff, the steel axe, the mithril square shield, fire and chaos runes and the odd gem.

places: Waterfall Dungeon - eleven of them, western passage and chalice room
Brimhaven Dungeon
Catacombs of Kourend
Stronghold Slayer Dungeon
Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
details: Strongest of the standard giants
Rune scimitar, about one in a hundred and twenty-eight by my tallies
Cannot be burned, weak to water spells

entries.name: Monk of Zamorak
entries.summary: Evil human clerics of Zamorak, god of chaos. Weak on paper, but the paper is wrong: they switch between melee and magic and hit harder than their level suggests. A band of them seized Paterdomus in Priest in Peril and poisoned the River Salve, which tells you the sort.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Described as "An evil human cleric." Brief, and fair. They serve Zamorak, god of chaos, and turn up at levels 17, 22, 23, 30 and 45.

Do not trust the level. They switch between melee and magic and hit harder than the number suggests.

They always leave bones. Zamorak monk robe tops and bottoms come about one in twenty, by my tallies.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Paterdomus, the temple on the River Salve, all through Priest in Peril. They had the run of the place.

Otherwise the Chaos Temple in Asgarnia, the cage under the stairs in Varrock Palace, Taverley Dungeon and the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
During Priest in Peril they occupied Paterdomus, the ground floor and everything above it, meaning to destroy the Salve's barrier. The hooded level 30 monk stood at the door and impersonated Drezel, the priest they had imprisoned. He had you kill the Temple Guardian, then dropped the golden key. The dog has its own page.

The temple monks regenerate quickly and give only 25 percent of normal combat experience. Poor value.

They were cleared out of the temple for good in The Blood Moon Rises. Many an adventurer trains magic on the caged one in Varrock Palace with the Curse spell. He is in no position to object.

people: Drezel - the priest they imprisoned, then impersonated
Zamorak - the god they serve. Chaos, by trade.
places: Paterdomus - taken and held during Priest in Peril
Chaos Temple in Asgarnia
Varrock Palace - one in a cage under the stairs
Taverley Dungeon
Deep Wilderness Dungeon
details: Temple monks give only 25 percent experience
Zamorak monk robes, top and bottom, about one in twenty by my tallies
Gone from Paterdomus for good after The Blood Moon Rises

entries.name: Temple Guardian
entries.summary: A big dog that lived in the mausoleum under Paterdomus and guarded the source of the River Salve, until the monks of Zamorak tricked you into killing it during Priest in Peril. It never comes back. Worth a page, I thought.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Described, and fairly, as "Looks like a big ugly dog." Level 30, 45 hitpoints, hits for 3 at most. Stabs, and quickly. The Slayer masters would count it among the dogs, for what that is worth.

Immune to magic and to dwarf cannons. Immune to poison and venom as well. Rings of recoil will do the job, so long as you land at least one hit yourself.

It never comes back.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
The mausoleum under Paterdomus, down the trapdoor north of the temple, during Priest in Peril.

It is killed in the course of the quest and never comes back. Found once, then.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
King Roald says it guarded the mausoleum entrance and the source of the Salve, and that with it dead anyone could sabotage the river's blessing. Which is exactly what the monks were after, and exactly why the impostor at the door had you do it.

Roald called it Spots. He also called it a pedigree light beast, or was it dark beast. His words, not mine.

It is said that Dark beasts once looked much like it, only brown. Make of that what you will.

people: King Roald - its owner. He called it Spots.
Monk of Zamorak - the impostor at the door who had you kill it
places: Mausoleum under Paterdomus - its only home
details: Never comes back
Immune to magic, and to dwarf cannons
Roald's name for it was Spots
Dark beasts once looked like it, only brown, or so it is said

plates.caption: Spots, as the King had it.

entries.name: Moss Guardian
entries.summary: The guardian spirits of Glarial's Tomb, and a good deal bigger and stronger than the ordinary moss giant. You slipped past them unarmed for Glarial's amulet and urn, and in Roving Elves you must go back and kill one bare-handed for a consecration seed. Bare-handed, noted.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Described as "Bigger than your average moss giant." Level 84, 120 hitpoints, hits up to 14, and slow to swing. Attack, Strength and Defence 60 each. Always aggressive.

Each blow is tried as ordinary melee first. If that misses, it is tried again against your magic defence. Protect from Melee stops only the first part. Underlined.

The tomb admits no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition, so they are fought with fists, food and potions. Drops are big bones and, during Roving Elves, the consecration seed.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
Glarial's Tomb, south-east of Baxtorian Falls and north-west of the Fishing Guild, under a tombstone. Three of them, and nowhere else.

The tomb admits no weapons, armour, runes or ammunition, so they are met with bare hands. Bring food.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
They guard Glarial, the queen whose tomb it is. You slipped past them unarmed for Glarial's amulet and urn, which was the sensible way to do it.

In Roving Elves, Islwyn and Eluned send you back to kill one. Still unarmed, by tomb rule. The consecration seed is what you go in for.

people: Glarial - the queen whose tomb they guard
Islwyn and Eluned - send you back to kill one in Roving Elves
places: Glarial's Tomb - their only home, under a tombstone
details: Fought unarmed, by tomb rule
Two tries per blow: melee, then magic if the melee misses
Drops the consecration seed in Roving Elves

entries.name: Lumbridge
entries.summary: A large town in Misthalin, where everyone begins and where the dead come back, so it gets a lot of traffic. It is named for the bridge over the River Lum. Duke Horacio rules from the castle.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Lumbridge is a large town in the kingdom of Misthalin, and it is where adventurers begin. Tutorial Island sends its new arrivals here. It is also where the dead come back to, unless they have arranged otherwise, so most people see it at least twice, once on the way in and once after the first mistake.

Duke Horacio rules from Lumbridge Castle. He is a direct descendant of Polonius, the first Duke. It is the kind of thing a duke likes written down, so I have.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body:
South of Varrock, east of Draynor Village, west of Al Kharid, with Lumbridge Swamp to the south.

Landmarks: the castle, the church of Saradomin, the cow field, the general store, and the swamp with its caves.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
In the year 1937 of the Fourth Age, long after the God Wars, migrating human nomads settled on the River Lum. They built a bridge across it, then named the town after the bridge. Practical people. Good bridge.

Father Aereck keeps the church of Saradomin, which is 230 years old and still standing. An unassuming shed in the swamp leads to the fairy city of Zanaris, once Lost City is done. I would not have guessed from the shed.

Quests that start here: Cook's Assistant, The Restless Ghost, Sheep Shearer and Rune Mysteries. Four scrolls from one town with one bridge.

people: Duke Horacio - rules Lumbridge from the castle, descendant of Polonius
Polonius - the first Duke of Lumbridge
Father Aereck - priest of the Saradomin church
The Lumbridge Guide - helps new adventurers and turns up in several quests
places: Lumbridge Castle - the Duke's seat and the town's landmark
Church of Lumbridge - a Saradomin church over 230 years old
River Lum - the river the bridge crosses, and the reason for the name
Lumbridge Swamp - south of town, with the caves and the shed to Zanaris
Zanaris - the fairy city reached from the swamp shed after Lost City
details: Founded in year 1937 of the Fourth Age by human nomads
Named for the bridge over the River Lum
Where the dead come back to, unless they have arranged otherwise
Where Tutorial Island sends new adventurers
Starting point of Cook's Assistant, The Restless Ghost, Sheep Shearer and Rune Mysteries

entries.name: Varrock
entries.summary: The capital of Misthalin and one of the largest cities in Gielinor. It began as Avarrocka, a tribal settlement named for a boy who drove off goblins, and King Roald now rules from the palace at its heart. Loud, busy, and I am fond of it.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Varrock, said vah-ROCK, is the capital of the kingdom of Misthalin. It is one of the largest cities in Gielinor. King Roald resides in Varrock Palace, the city's focal point. You cannot miss it, though people try.

Inside the walls: the Grand Exchange, the Varrock Museum, the Champions' Guild, the Blue Moon Inn, a Saradomin church and a Zamorakian chapel. Both faiths, one set of walls. I have not asked how that works. Beneath it all run the sewers, where Scurrius and Bryophyta lurk.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Central Misthalin. The Wilderness lies to the north, Barbarian Village to the north-west, the Digsite to the east and Lumbridge to the south.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
The city was founded as Avarrocka in year 700 of the Fourth Age. A nomadic tribe found a boy of exceptional strength and settled in the forest there. Ten years later goblins attacked.

The boy defeated them and became known as Arrav, and as Arrav grew, so did Avarrocka. The name has shortened since. The boy has not been forgotten.

Zemouregal, a Zamorakian Mahjarrat necromancer, later invaded with an army of zombies. His forces were beaten, but Arrav fell and was taken as an undead servant. A poor ending for the boy. The city rebuilt, grew into the kingdom of Misthalin and became a monarchy.

The Shield of Arrav still figures in city lore. Quests that start here: Demon Slayer, Dragon Slayer I, Romeo & Juliet, Shield of Arrav, Defender of Varrock, Family Crest and Priest in Peril. A busy notice board, and I have stood at it a while.

Arrav - the boy hero the city is named after, later raised as Zemouregal's undead servant
Zemouregal - Zamorakian Mahjarrat necromancer who invaded Avarrocka with zombies

Grand Exchange - the great trading floor
Varrock Museum - natural history displays and a quiz
Champions' Guild - sells rune weapons and green dragonhide
Blue Moon Inn - the most popular pub in Varrock

Named for Arrav, who as a boy defeated attacking goblins
Zemouregal's zombie invasion killed Arrav and raised him undead

A Saradomin church and a Zamorakian chapel, both inside the walls

plates.caption: The square. Only we stood still.
King Roald. I bowed, to be safe.

entries.name: Paterdomus
entries.summary: The temple of Saradomin on the River Salve, at the eastern edge of Misthalin. It is the only gate into Morytania, and it stands over the graves of the Seven Priestly Warriors, on the spot where they blessed the river. I lower my voice in there.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
The name comes from an old tongue, pater plus domus. House of the Father, meaning Saradomin. Its bridge is the only crossing of the Salve, and you need Drezel's blessing to use it. He is the temple's only monk, so there is no one else to ask.

Four floors: an altar on the ground floor, monks of Zamorak above it, and Drezel's old cell and a vampyre coffin at the top. Monks of Zamorak in a house of Saradomin is not what you expect, but there it is. A trapdoor to the north leads down to the basement mausoleum: the guardian's chamber, a well ringed by seven monuments, a hidden library, and the passage where Drezel now lives.

Outside are more coffins. They hold vampyres stranded west of the river, too weak to move and impossible to kill, which is a combination I do not care for. There is a statue of Saradomin by the water, and a railing shortcut at 65 Agility.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Eastern Silvarea, on the River Salve, at the eastern edge of Misthalin. Silvarea is the pass that leads to it. Canifis is just across the river.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
During the Misthalin-Morytania War the Seven Priestly Warriors held Drakan's horde here and performed the blood ritual that blessed the Salve. Six of them died. Ivandis Seergaze buried them around the well, and the temple rose over the site. So the well in the mausoleum has the six of them lying round it, and I mind where I stand.

The monks of Zamorak occupied the temple until The Blood Moon Rises. It features in Priest in Peril, Nature Spirit, In Aid of the Myreque, Darkness of Hallowvale, Sins of the Father, Devious Minds and The Blood Moon Rises, and it is the finish line of Temple Trekking. A great many scrolls pass through this door. Mine included.

Seven Priestly Warriors - buried beneath it, around the well
Monks of Zamorak - occupied it until The Blood Moon Rises

River Salve - flows beneath the bridge
Mausoleum - the basement, down the trapdoor to the north
Canifis - just across the river

entries.name: Baxtorian Falls
entries.summary: Rapids in Kandarin, running south from the Lunar Sea to the River Dougne, north-west of Ardougne. Named for the elven king who sealed himself beneath them, which tells you something about the place. Almera's raft, Glarial's tomb and the Waterfall Dungeon are all here.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
A stretch of rapids with a great deal packed around it, starting with Almera and Hudon, who live at the top. Hadley's Tourist Information Centre and Gerald the fisherman are just south. Rasolo the merchant is nearby, and overpriced. I checked.

The raft by Almera's house drops you on the island in the river. From there a rope on the rock and dead tree leads down to the Waterfall Dungeon, Baxtorian's sealed home, with its fire giants and the Chalice of Eternity. Glarial's Tomb is a short way south-east, under a tombstone. There is a monument with a statue of Baxtorian, and a second waterfall that flows east from the lake.

The west bank is for leaping-fish Barbarian fishing, which is fast Fishing training with a Barbarian rod. After Barbarian Training, the whirlpool takes you down into the Ancient Cavern. On purpose, I am assured.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: Kandarin, north-west of Ardougne. East of the Tree Gnome Stronghold and south of the Barbarian Outpost. The falls run south from the Lunar Sea to the River Dougne. Get there by games necklace, or on foot from Seers' Village if you want the walk.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body: The falls are named for Lord Baxtorian Cadarn, the elven king who sealed himself beneath them. The dungeon is his home, and he locked the door from the inside. There is a barrel that leads down into the dungeon as well. I took the rope.

entries.name: Seven Priestly Warriors
entries.summary: Seven Temple Knights of the Fourth Age, who stopped Lord Drakan's vampyres at the River Salve and blessed the river so no vampyre could cross it. Six died doing it. The last, Ivandis Seergaze, buried the others where Paterdomus now stands.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Seven Temple Knights: Ivandis Seergaze, Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious, Friar Twiblick and Essiandar Gar. Active around 1200 of the Fourth Age, during the Misthalin-Morytania War. I have written all seven names out in full. They earned that much.

The Temple Knights sent them to secure the Salve. Secretly, they were also to research haemalchemy, which their leaders believed held the key to beating vampyres.

Their savants designed a blood ritual to bar vampyres from the river. The warriors hid its profane nature from the soldiers and called it a holy consecration by Saradomin. A blood rite with a clean name. It worked, which is the uncomfortable part.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
At the river's source the vampyres attacked mid-ritual. Derygull fell first, then the others, one by one. Only Ivandis survived. He laid the six to rest around the ritual well, and the temple built around it is Paterdomus.

Ivandis was showing signs of vampyrification. He refused to become what they had sworn to destroy, and charged into Morytania to kill Drakan. He died in the attempt, and his coffin lies in caves beneath the Hollows. I have no remark for that one.

Later histories say the blessing sealed the vengeful power of Saradomin in the river. Drezel of Paterdomus is descended from one of the seven, and Ivan Strom is Ivandis's last living descendant.

entries.name: Morytania
entries.summary: A land of evil in the far east of Gielinor, ruled by vampyres under Lord Drakan. It was the Saradominist kingdom of Hallowvale once, until he drained it into swamp and used the people as a blood farm. Only the blessed River Salve keeps the vampyres out of Misthalin, and I am fond of that river.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Morytania, said mor-ee-TAY-nee-ah, is a region in the easternmost part of Gielinor. It is full of aggressive creatures and ruled over by the vampyres. Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan leads them, and his siblings Vanescula and Ranis handle the running of things. Darkmeyer is the capital.

The towns, none of them restful: Canifis, home to werewolves; Port Phasmatys, a cursed port of ghosts; Mort'ton, plague-stricken; Burgh de Rott, the last free human settlement; Slepe, a Zamorakian town; and Meiyerditch, a blood farm for the vampyres. Mort Myre Swamp, the Haunted Woods and the Barrows lie between them, so the walks are no better than the stops.

sections.heading: Where it is found
sections.body: East of Misthalin, across the River Salve. The way in is the temple of Paterdomus on the river, and you must complete Priest in Peril before you can pass. Canifis is the first town east of the temple.

sections.heading: Worth knowing
sections.body:
Before the God Wars this was Hallowvale, a Saradominist kingdom ruled by the Icyene Queen Efaritay. In the Third Age the vampyre Lord Drakan conquered it. He turned the fertile land into swamp and kept its people as a blood farm. That is the history of the place in three sentences, and none of them get better.

Around year 1100 of the Fourth Age the Seven Priestly Warriors, led by Ivandis Seergaze, held Misthalin against Drakan's invasion and blessed the River Salve. The barrier they raised holds to this day. Vampyres cannot cross it. I check, every time.

The Barrows brothers, empowered by the Mahjarrat Sliske, tried to liberate the land. They were betrayed, their powers stripped at the gates of Darkmeyer, and slaughtered. The Myreque now fight to throw off vampyre rule. I hope they get a longer page than the brothers did.
